eyebrow: How Things Work · 萬物原理
lead_en: Everyday questions with surprising answers: how batteries store power, how a message crosses the ocean, why the sky is blue. Read the answer in English, then see it work in 3D.
lead_zh: 生活裡的問題，背後都有驚人的答案：電池怎麼存電、訊息怎麼橫越大海、天空為什麼是藍的。先用英文讀懂，再用 3D 看它怎麼運作。

intro.en: Every lesson starts with an everyday question. A 3D model shows the answer at work, one idea at a time, and an English reading explains it, with Chinese a tap away.
intro.zh: 每一課都從一個生活裡的問題開始：先用 3D 模型看答案怎麼運作，一課只講清楚一個道理；再讀一篇英文短文把它說明白，中文翻譯隨點隨看。

intro.en: The lessons are grouped into five units. Each lesson has words to learn, a short quiz, common myths, easy ways to remember the idea, and an activity to try at home or in class. Facts and numbers are checked, and every lesson lists its sources.
intro.zh: 課程分成五個單元。每一課都有生字、小測驗、常見迷思、記憶口訣，以及在家或在教室就能做的活動。事實與數字都經過查證，每課最後列出資料出處。

units.blurb_en: Where the power in your pocket, your wall, and on your roof comes from.
units.blurb_zh: 口袋裡、插座裡、屋頂上的電，都是從哪裡來的。

lessons.title: How Does a Battery Store Electricity?
lessons.blurb_en: A battery is not a tank of electricity. Look inside a lithium-ion battery in 3D and watch ions cross inside while electrons light the bulb outside.
lessons.blurb_zh: 電池不是裝著電的罐子。用 3D 看進鋰離子電池裡：離子在裡面跨過去，電子在外面點亮燈泡。
lessons.big_idea_en: A battery does not hold electricity. It holds two chemicals that want to trade electrons. Close the circuit, and the electrons flow through the wire outside. That flow is electricity.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 電池裡裝的不是電，而是兩種想交換電子的化學物質。把電路接通，電子就從外面的電線流過去，這股流動就是電。

lab.how_en: Drag to turn the model, and scroll or pinch to zoom. Choose Use it, Charge it, or Switch off, and watch the yellow lithium ions inside and the blue electrons in the wire. Drag the Charge slider to set the battery level, and the Charge cycles slider to make the battery older.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉模型，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。選「用電」「充電」或「關掉」，看黃色的鋰離子在電池裡移動、藍色的電子在電線裡移動。拖動「電量」滑桿可以設定電量，拖動「充放電循環」滑桿可以讓電池變老。

legend.en: Blue beads: electrons (e⁻) in the wire
legend.zh: 藍色小珠：電線裡的電子

legend.en: Gray balls: lithium trapped in the crust on the graphite (old battery)
legend.zh: 灰色球：被困在石墨表面薄殼裡的鋰（老電池）

lab.scale_en: A diagram, not to scale. The front is cut away; a real battery is sealed. Real electrodes are thinner than paper and rolled up tightly, and they hold billions of billions of lithium ions, not seventy. In a real wire, electrons drift far more slowly than shown here. The voltage and the 80% figure follow the sources listed at the bottom of the page.
lab.scale_zh: 這是示意圖，大小不按比例。正面是剖開的，真正的電池是密封的；真實的電極比紙還薄、捲得很緊，裡面的鋰離子是幾十億的幾十億倍，不是七十顆。真實電線裡電子漂移的速度比這裡慢得多。電壓與「80%」的數字依照頁面最下方列出的出處。
lab.credit_html: Model drawn by My Culture Connect as a teaching diagram. Battery behavior is simplified from Battery University BU-204; capacity loss follows Apple's figure of 80% after 500 full cycles, drawn as a straight line. · 模型由人師教育協會自繪示意；電池行為簡化自 Battery University，容量衰退依 Apple 公布的「500 次完整循環後保有 80%」畫成直線。

paras: Look at the top corner of your phone. Maybe it says 73%. In a few hours it might say 20%, and the phone will warn you to charge it. But what exactly is running out? Most people picture a battery as a little tank of electricity, like a bottle of water that slowly empties. That picture is wrong, and the real answer is much more interesting.

The first battery was built in 1800 by the Italian scientist Alessandro Volta. He stacked discs of zinc and copper with cloth soaked in salt water between them. Every battery since then, including the one in your phone, works on the same idea. A battery holds two different chemicals, one at each end. One side has electrons it would like to give away, and the other side would like to take them. A battery is not a box of electricity. It is a box of chemicals that want to trade electrons.

So why don't the electrons just jump across inside the battery? Between the two sides sits a material called the electrolyte. It lets charged atoms, called ions, pass through, but it blocks electrons. The electrons are stuck. They can only reach the other side if you give them a path outside the battery. That path is a circuit: a wire from one end of the battery, through a light bulb or the parts of your phone, and back to the other end.

When the circuit is closed, electrons flow out of the negative end, through the wire, and into the positive end. That flow of electrons is electricity, and on its way it lights the bulb or runs your phone. At the same time, inside the battery, ions move through the electrolyte to keep both sides balanced: one ion inside for every electron outside. Open the circuit, and both flows stop at once. That is why a battery can sit in a drawer for months and still work.

Your phone has a lithium-ion battery. Its negative side is graphite, the same material as pencil lead, made of thin layers like the floors of a parking garage. When the battery is charged, lithium is parked between those layers. As you use the phone, lithium ions leave the graphite, cross the electrolyte, and settle into the layers of a metal oxide on the positive side, while their electrons take the long way through the phone. Charging pushes them all back. The scientists who developed this battery shared the 2019 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

So what does 73% mean? Your phone estimates how much of the lithium that can move is still waiting in the graphite. And why does an old phone die faster? Each time you charge and use it, a few lithium ions get trapped in a thin crust that slowly grows on the graphite, and they never move again. Heat makes the crust grow faster, and so does keeping the battery full for long periods. Many phones are designed to keep about 80% of their original capacity after 500 full charge cycles. The phone still says 100% when it is full, but its full is smaller than it used to be.
paras_zh: 看看你手機螢幕上方的角落，也許顯示 73%。再過幾個小時可能剩 20%，手機會提醒你充電。可是，到底是什麼東西在「用完」？大多數人把電池想像成一個裝電的小罐子，像一瓶水慢慢被倒空。這個畫面是錯的，真正的答案有趣得多。
第一顆電池是義大利科學家伏打在 1800 年做出來的。他把鋅片和銅片疊起來，中間夾著泡過鹽水的布。從那以後的每一顆電池，包括你手機裡那顆，都是同一個道理：電池裡有兩種不同的化學物質，一頭一種。一邊有想送出去的電子，另一邊想要接收電子。電池不是一盒電，而是一盒想交換電子的化學物質。
那電子為什麼不直接在電池裡面跳過去？因為兩邊中間隔著一種叫做「電解液」的材料。它讓帶電的原子，也就是「離子」通過，卻擋住電子。電子被卡住了，只有在電池外面給它一條路，它才到得了另一邊。這條路就是電路：一條電線從電池的一頭出發，經過燈泡或手機裡的零件，再回到另一頭。
電路接通時，電子從負極流出來，經過電線，流進正極。這股電子的流動就是電，一路上它點亮燈泡、讓手機運作。同時，在電池裡面，離子穿過電解液，讓兩邊保持平衡：外面每走一個電子，裡面就走一顆離子。把電路斷開，兩股流動會同時停下來。所以電池放在抽屜裡好幾個月，拿出來還能用。
你的手機用的是鋰離子電池。它的負極是石墨，跟鉛筆芯是同一種材料，由一層層薄片組成，像立體停車場的樓層。電池充滿電時，鋰就停在這些層與層之間。你使用手機時，鋰離子離開石墨、穿過電解液，住進正極那邊金屬氧化物的層間；它們的電子則繞遠路，經過整支手機。充電就是把它們全部推回去。發展出這種電池的科學家，共同獲得了 2019 年諾貝爾化學獎。
那 73% 是什麼意思？手機在估計：能移動的鋰，還有多少留在石墨裡等著。那為什麼舊手機的電用得比較快？每次充電和使用，都會有幾顆鋰離子被困在石墨表面一層慢慢長厚的薄殼裡，從此再也不能移動。高溫會讓這層殼長得更快，長時間一直充滿電也會。許多手機的設計是：完整充放電 500 次以後，還保有原本大約 80% 的容量。電池充滿時手機一樣顯示 100%，只是這個「滿」比以前小了。
questions: Why can't the electrons simply move from one side to the other inside the battery?
When you use your phone, what moves inside the battery, and what moves through the wire?
Why does an old phone battery run out faster than a new one?
answers: Because the electrolyte between the two sides lets ions through but blocks electrons. The electrons can only cross through a circuit outside the battery.
Inside, lithium ions move from the graphite through the electrolyte to the metal oxide. Through the wire, electrons move from the negative end to the positive end, one electron for every ion.

Every time the battery is charged and used, some lithium gets trapped in a thin crust on the graphite, so less lithium can move. A full charge holds less than it did when the battery was new. Heat and staying full for long periods make this happen faster.

vocab.ex: Every atom has tiny electrons moving around its center.
vocab.exzh: 每個原子都有微小的電子在它的中心周圍移動。

vocab.ex: Some chemicals under the sink are dangerous, so keep them away from small children.
vocab.exzh: 水槽下面有些化學物質很危險，要放在小孩拿不到的地方。

vocab.ex: The electrolyte in a car battery is a strong acid.
vocab.exzh: 汽車電瓶裡的電解液是強酸。

vocab.ex: Salt water carries electricity because it is full of ions.
vocab.exzh: 鹽水能導電，因為裡面充滿了離子。

vocab.ex: The light didn't turn on because the circuit was broken.
vocab.exzh: 燈沒有亮，因為電路斷了。

vocab.ex: Rivers flow from the mountains to the sea.
I charge my phone every night before I go to bed.
vocab.exzh: 我每天晚上睡覺前都會幫手機充電。

vocab.ex: This water bottle has a capacity of one liter.
vocab.exzh: 這個水壺的容量是一公升。

quiz.q: What does a battery actually store?
options: Two chemicals that want to trade electrons
It lets ions through but blocks electrons
It lets electrons through but blocks ions
It makes the battery heavier so it won't move

quiz.q: When you use your phone, which way do the electrons in the wire flow?
options: From the negative end to the positive end
From the positive end to the negative end
They do not move at all

quiz.q: In a charged lithium-ion battery, where is most of the lithium that can move?
Why does an old phone battery hold less charge?
options: Some lithium gets trapped and can no longer move
Electricity leaks out into your pocket
The phone shows the wrong number on purpose

parts.text_en: A stack of carbon sheets with room between them. When the battery is charged, lithium is parked in those gaps, ready to give away its electrons.
parts.text_zh: 一疊碳的薄片，片與片之間留有空間。電池充滿時，鋰就停在這些空隙裡，隨時準備送出電子。

parts.meta_en: Metals such as cobalt or nickel, joined with oxygen
parts.text_en: Layers that lithium would rather live in. As you use the battery, lithium ions move in here, and the electrons that went around the wire join them.
parts.text_zh: 鋰比較「想住」的層狀材料。使用電池時，鋰離子搬進這裡，繞過電線的電子也在這裡和它們會合。

parts.meta_en: A lithium salt dissolved in a liquid
parts.text_en: The road for ions. It lets lithium ions pass but blocks electrons, which forces the electrons to take the wire. It can burn, which is one reason a lithium battery must never be punctured.
parts.text_zh: 離子走的路。它讓鋰離子通過、擋住電子，逼電子去走電線。它會燃燒，這也是鋰電池絕對不能刺破的原因之一。

parts.meta_en: A plastic film full of tiny holes
parts.text_en: A wall thinner than a hair that keeps the two sides from touching. If they touched, the battery would short-circuit and could overheat. Ions slip through its tiny holes.
parts.text_zh: 比頭髮還薄的一道牆，讓兩極不會碰在一起。要是碰到了，電池會短路，可能過熱。離子從它的小孔鑽過去。

lessons.parts_note_en: In a real phone battery, these layers are thinner than paper and are rolled or folded together many times over. The model shows just one slice.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 真正的手機電池裡，這幾層都比紙還薄，而且捲起來或摺疊了很多層。模型只畫出其中一個切面。

myths.myth_en: A battery is a container full of electricity.
myths.myth_zh: 電池是一個裝滿電的容器。
myths.fact_en: A battery stores chemicals, not electricity. When it runs down, the number of electrons inside does not change; what changes is where the lithium sits. Electricity only appears when a circuit lets electrons flow.
myths.fact_zh: 電池存的是化學物質，不是電。電池沒電時，裡面的電子數量並沒有變少，改變的是鋰待在哪一邊。要等電路讓電子流動，才有電。

myths.myth_en: Electrons race out of the battery at nearly the speed of light.
myths.myth_zh: 電子以接近光速從電池衝出去。
myths.fact_en: The wire is already full of electrons, and they all start shuffling forward at once, so the light comes on instantly. Each electron drifts slowly, usually less than a millimeter per second.
myths.fact_zh: 電線裡本來就塞滿電子，一接通它們就同時往前挪，所以燈馬上亮。每個電子其實走得很慢，通常一秒不到一毫米。

myths.myth_en: You should run a phone battery down to 0% before charging it.
myths.myth_zh: 手機電池要用到 0% 再充電。
myths.fact_en: That advice was for some older kinds of batteries. Lithium-ion batteries have no memory, and running them all the way down is hard on them. Charging whenever it is convenient is fine.
myths.fact_zh: 那是某些舊式電池的說法。鋰離子電池沒有「記憶效應」，每次都用到底反而傷電池。方便的時候就充，完全沒問題。

myths.myth_en: In a lemon battery, the lemon makes the electricity.
myths.myth_zh: 檸檬電池的電是檸檬做出來的。
myths.fact_en: The energy comes from the zinc slowly dissolving. The lemon juice is only the electrolyte. A potato or a cup of salt water works too.
myths.fact_zh: 能量來自鋅慢慢溶解。檸檬汁只是電解液，換成馬鈴薯或一杯鹽水也可以。

tricks.title_zh: 離子走裡面，電子走外面
tricks.body_en: Inside the battery, ions cross the electrolyte. Outside, electrons go around the wire. One for one, always together.
tricks.body_zh: 電池裡面，離子穿過電解液；電池外面，電子繞著電線走。一個對一個，永遠一起動。

tricks.body_en: Break the circuit anywhere and everything stops, inside and outside. That is all an on-off switch does.
tricks.body_zh: 電路在任何一處斷開，裡外的流動就全部停下來。開關做的就是這件事。

tricks.title_en: Charging pushes uphill, using rolls downhill
tricks.title_zh: 充電是推上坡，用電是滾下坡
tricks.body_en: Charging pushes lithium back into the graphite, where it doesn't want to be. Using the battery lets it roll back down, and the energy comes out as electricity.
tricks.body_zh: 充電把鋰推回它不想待的石墨裡；用電時讓它滾回去，能量就變成電放出來。

tricks.title_en: Keep it cool, keep it in the middle
tricks.title_zh: 保持涼爽，別老停在兩端
tricks.body_en: Heat, and sitting at 100% or 0% for a long time, wear a battery out faster. Room temperature and a charge somewhere in the middle are easiest on it.
tricks.body_zh: 高溫、長時間停在 100% 或 0%，都會讓電池老得比較快。室溫、電量在中間，對電池最輕鬆。

materials.zh: 3 到 4 顆新鮮多汁的檸檬

materials.en: 3 or 4 copper strips (or pieces of thick copper wire)
materials.zh: 3 到 4 片銅片（或粗銅線）

materials.en: 1 small red LED (red needs the least voltage)
materials.zh: 1 顆小的紅色 LED（紅色需要的電壓最低）

materials.en: A multimeter, if you have one

steps.en: Roll each lemon on the table, pressing down gently, to break up the juice inside.
steps.zh: 把每顆檸檬放在桌上輕壓滾一滾，讓裡面的果汁流出來。

steps.en: Push one copper strip and one zinc nail into each lemon, about 2 to 3 centimeters apart. They must not touch each other.
steps.zh: 在每顆檸檬插一片銅片和一根鍍鋅釘，相距約 2 到 3 公分，兩者不能碰在一起。

steps.en: If you have a multimeter, measure one lemon. You should see about 0.9 volts. Copper is the positive (+) side, and zinc is the negative (−) side.
steps.zh: 有三用電表的話，量一顆檸檬，大約是 0.9 伏特。銅是正極（+），鋅是負極（−）。

steps.en: Connect the lemons in a row: the zinc of lemon 1 to the copper of lemon 2, the zinc of lemon 2 to the copper of lemon 3, and so on. This is called connecting them in series, and the voltages add up.
steps.zh: 把檸檬串成一排：第一顆的鋅接第二顆的銅、第二顆的鋅接第三顆的銅，以此類推。這叫「串聯」，電壓會加起來。

steps.en: Clip the free copper (+) to the LED's long leg and the free zinc (−) to its short leg. Turn off the room lights and look closely. A red LED usually needs two or three lemons in a row; if it stays dark, add another lemon or check the LED's legs.
steps.zh: 把最後剩下的銅（+）接到 LED 的長腳，鋅（−）接到短腳。關掉教室的燈仔細看。紅色 LED 通常要串兩、三顆檸檬；如果不亮，再加一顆，或檢查 LED 有沒有接反。

steps.en: Talk about it: which metal is being used up? (The zinc slowly dissolves, and tiny bubbles of hydrogen form on the copper.)
steps.zh: 討論：哪一種金屬在被消耗？（鋅慢慢溶解，銅片上會冒出很小的氫氣泡。）

activities.tip_en: Safety: an adult should do any cutting, and the lemons must go in the trash afterward, never in anyone's mouth, because metal has dissolved into the juice. Wash your hands when you finish. A lemon battery gives only a tiny current, about a thousandth of an amp at most, so it can light a small LED dimly but can never charge a phone. Never try any of this with a wall outlet.
activities.tip_zh: 安全：需要切東西時由大人來做；做完的檸檬一律丟掉，絕對不能吃，因為金屬已經溶進果汁裡。做完要洗手。檸檬電池的電流很小，最多大約千分之一安培，只能讓小 LED 微微發亮，絕對不能幫手機充電。也絕對不要拿插座做任何實驗。

activities.title_en: Pass the Electrons: A Human Battery

materials.en: About 12 soft balls or beanbags (the electrons)
materials.zh: 大約 12 顆軟球或沙包（電子）

materials.en: Yellow paper badges for 4 students (the lithium)

steps.en: Students stand in a big loop. On one half of the loop, each student holds one ball. This half is the wire, and it is already full of electrons.
steps.zh: 全班站成一個大圈。圈的一半，每個人手上拿一顆球——這一半是電線，裡面本來就裝滿了電子。

steps.en: Inside the loop, the graphite team stands on the left and the metal oxide team on the right, with the chairs between them. The four lithium students start with the graphite team.
steps.zh: 圈內左邊站「石墨隊」、右邊站「金屬氧化物隊」，中間隔著那排椅子。四位「鋰」同學一開始站在石墨隊。

steps.en: The rule: a lithium student may walk across the chairs only when, at the same moment, every student in the wire passes a ball one place toward the metal oxide side. Balls may never cross the chairs.
steps.zh: 規則：只有在電線上每個人同時把球往金屬氧化物那邊傳一格的那一刻，一位鋰同學才可以越過椅子。球永遠不准越過椅子。

steps.en: One student in the wire is the bulb and claps each time a ball passes. That clap is the light.
steps.zh: 電線上有一位同學當燈泡，每有一顆球經過就拍一次手——那就是燈亮。

steps.en: Now charge it: the teacher is the charger and makes the wire pass balls backward, and the lithium students walk back to the graphite.
steps.zh: 接著充電：老師當充電器，讓電線上的球往回傳，鋰同學走回石墨隊。

steps.en: Ask: what happens if one student in the wire refuses to pass? Everyone freezes. That is a switch, and that is why a battery keeps its charge on the shelf.
steps.zh: 問大家：如果電線上有一個人不肯傳球，會怎樣？全部停住。這就是開關，也是電池放著不會沒電的原因。

activities.tip_en: The game shows the two big ideas of this lesson: ions travel inside and electrons travel outside, and they always move together, one for one. It also shows why a light comes on instantly even though each ball moves only one place.
activities.tip_zh: 這個遊戲演出本課的兩個大觀念：離子走裡面、電子走外面，而且永遠一個對一個一起動。它也說明了為什麼每顆球只移動一格，燈卻馬上就亮。

safety.en: Never open, puncture, crush, or bend a lithium battery. Its electrolyte can burn, and a damaged battery can catch fire.
safety.zh: 絕不拆開、刺穿、壓扁或彎折鋰電池。它的電解液會燃燒，受損的電池可能起火。

safety.en: If a phone or power bank becomes puffy, very hot, or smells strange, stop using and charging it, and tell an adult.
safety.zh: 手機或行動電源如果鼓起來、變得很燙或有怪味，立刻停止使用和充電，並告訴大人。

safety.en: Never do experiments with a wall outlet. The electricity in the wall can seriously hurt or kill you. The activities on this page use only lemons and tiny currents.
safety.zh: 絕對不要拿插座做實驗。插座裡的電會造成重傷甚至致命。本頁的活動只用檸檬和非常小的電流。

safety.en: Keep button batteries away from young children. A swallowed button battery can cause severe burns in as little as two hours. If you think a child swallowed one, get medical help right away.
safety.zh: 鈕扣電池要放在幼兒拿不到的地方。吞下去的鈕扣電池最快兩小時就能造成嚴重灼傷；懷疑孩子吞了，要立刻就醫。

safety.en: Do not throw batteries in the trash. In Taiwan, convenience stores, supermarkets, and recycling trucks collect used batteries. Cover the ends of lithium batteries with tape first.
safety.zh: 電池不要丟一般垃圾。在台灣，便利商店、超市和資源回收車都收廢電池。鋰電池的兩極先用膠帶貼起來再回收。

sources.en: Volta's first battery, 1800
sources.zh: 伏打的第一顆電池（1800 年）

sources.en: The 2019 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for lithium-ion batteries
sources.zh: 2019 年諾貝爾化學獎：鋰離子電池

sources.en: How lithium-ion batteries work; about 3.6 volts per cell; no memory effect
sources.zh: 鋰離子電池原理、每顆約 3.6 伏特、沒有記憶效應

sources.en: Heat and staying fully charged wear batteries out faster
sources.zh: 高溫與長時間充滿會加速電池老化

sources.en: The crust on the graphite (SEI) is the main cause of capacity loss
sources.zh: 石墨表面的薄殼（SEI）是容量衰退的主因

sources.en: 80% of original capacity after 500 full cycles (iPhone 14 and earlier; iPhone 15 and later: 1,000 cycles)
sources.zh: 500 次完整循環後保有 80% 容量（iPhone 14 以前；iPhone 15 以後為 1,000 次）

sources.en: Electrons drift less than a millimeter per second
sources.zh: 電子漂移每秒不到一毫米

sources.en: Lemon battery: about 0.9 volts, energy from the zinc
sources.zh: 檸檬電池約 0.9 伏特，能量來自鋅

sources.en: Button batteries can cause severe burns within two hours
sources.zh: 鈕扣電池兩小時內可造成嚴重灼傷

sources.en: Taping the ends of used lithium batteries
sources.zh: 廢鋰電池兩極貼膠帶

sources.en: Where to recycle batteries in Taiwan
sources.zh: 台灣的廢電池回收管道
sources.src: 桃園市政府環境保護局

lessons.title: Where Does the Electricity in the Wall Come From?
lessons.blurb_en: Every outlet is connected to a spinning magnet. Turn the generator in 3D, watch the current swing back and forth, and see where Taiwan's power comes from.
lessons.blurb_zh: 每一個插座，另一頭都連著一塊轉動的磁鐵。用 3D 轉轉看發電機，看電流來回擺動，再看看台灣的電從哪裡來。
lessons.big_idea_en: Almost all the electricity in the wall comes from a magnet spinning past coils of wire in a power plant. Steam, gas, water, or wind only does one job: it keeps the magnet turning.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 插座裡的電，幾乎都來自發電廠裡一塊在線圈旁邊轉動的磁鐵。蒸汽、燃氣、水或風只做一件事：讓磁鐵一直轉。

lab.how_en: Drag to turn the model, and scroll or pinch to zoom. Pick what turns the shaft, or choose Your hand and hold the button to crank it yourself. Drag the Spin speed slider down to zero and watch everything stop. The graph shows the voltage swinging between plus and minus.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉模型，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。選擇是什麼在轉動轉軸，或選「你的手」、按住按鈕自己搖。把「轉速」滑桿拉到零，看一切停下來。右邊的圖顯示電壓在正負之間來回擺動。

legend.en: Red and blue bar: the magnet's north (N) and south (S) poles
legend.zh: 紅藍磁棒：磁鐵的 N 極與 S 極

legend.en: Copper rings: coils of wire. They glow when current flows.
legend.zh: 銅色環：線圈；有電流時會發亮

legend.en: Blue beads and arrows: electrons in the wire and the direction they are pushed
legend.zh: 藍色小珠與箭頭：電線裡的電子和它被推的方向

lab.scale_en: A diagram, not to scale. Real power plant generators use electromagnets and three sets of coils, weigh hundreds of tons, and in Taiwan spin 60 times a second (3,600 turns a minute for a two-pole generator). Here the speed is slowed down so you can see each turn. The power lines, substations, and transformers between the plant and your home are left out; see the reading.
lab.scale_zh: 這是示意圖，大小不按比例。真正電廠的發電機用的是電磁鐵和三組線圈，重達數百公噸，在台灣每秒轉 60 圈（兩極發電機每分鐘 3,600 圈）；這裡放慢到看得清每一圈。電廠和你家之間的輸電線、變電所、變壓器沒有畫出來，請看課文。
lab.credit_html: Model drawn by My Culture Connect as a teaching diagram, following the generator explanation of the U.S. Energy Information Administration. · 模型由人師教育協會自繪示意，發電原理依美國能源資訊署的說明。

paras: Plug in a phone charger, and electricity is there instantly, day and night. A battery runs out, but the outlet in the wall never seems to. Where does that electricity come from? Follow the wires behind the wall, and they lead to a power line, then to a substation, and finally to a power plant that may be far away. And inside almost every power plant, you will find the same simple thing: a magnet that spins.

In 1831, the English scientist Michael Faraday discovered something amazing. When he moved a magnet near a coil of wire, electricity flowed in the wire. When the magnet stopped, the electricity stopped too. A magnet sitting still does nothing; it is the change, the movement, that pushes the electrons. This is called electromagnetic induction, and almost every power plant in the world depends on it.

A generator is a faster, bigger version of Faraday's experiment. A magnet spins next to coils of wire. As the north pole sweeps past a coil, it pushes the electrons one way. Half a turn later, the south pole sweeps past and pushes them the other way. So the current keeps changing direction. This is called alternating current, or AC. In Taiwan, the current makes 60 complete back-and-forth cycles every second, which is why we say the power is 60 hertz.

So what turns the magnet? In most power plants, it is a turbine, a wheel with blades, pushed by something moving fast. Coal and nuclear plants boil water into high-pressure steam that blasts through the turbine. Gas plants burn natural gas in a turbine like a jet engine, and many also use the leftover heat to make steam. At a dam, falling water turns the turbine, and on a wind farm, the wind does. Only one common source works differently: solar panels turn sunlight into electricity with no moving parts at all.

From the generator, electricity travels across the island on tall towers. To travel far with little waste, it is raised to a very high voltage; Taipower's biggest lines carry 345,000 volts. Substations step it down again and again, until a transformer near your street lowers it to the 110 volts in your outlet. The electrons in your wall do not travel all the way from the power plant. They just wiggle back and forth in place while the energy rushes along the wires.

So where does Taiwan's electricity come from? In 2025, about 48% came from burning natural gas, 35% from coal, 13% from renewable sources such as solar and wind, and about 1% from nuclear power. Taiwan's last nuclear reactor shut down in May 2025. Every choice has a cost: coal and gas release carbon dioxide, and the sun and wind come and go with the weather. But apart from solar panels, all of them come back to the idea Faraday found almost two hundred years ago: spin a magnet, and the electrons move.
paras_zh: 插上手機充電器，電馬上就來了，白天晚上都一樣。電池會用完，牆上的插座卻好像永遠用不完。這些電是從哪裡來的？順著牆裡的電線往外找，會接到電線桿上的電線，再接到變電所，最後到達可能很遠很遠的發電廠。而幾乎每一座發電廠裡，都有同一樣簡單的東西：一塊會轉的磁鐵。
1831 年，英國科學家法拉第發現了一件驚人的事：他把磁鐵在一圈線圈旁邊移動，線圈裡就有電流；磁鐵一停，電也跟著停。磁鐵靜靜放著什麼都不會發生，是「變化」、是「動」在推電子。這叫做電磁感應，世界上幾乎每一座發電廠都靠它。
發電機就是法拉第實驗的放大、加速版：一塊磁鐵在線圈旁邊轉。N 極掃過線圈時，把電子往一個方向推；轉了半圈，換 S 極掃過，又把電子往反方向推。所以電流的方向一直在改變，這叫做交流電（AC）。在台灣，電流每秒完整來回 60 次，所以我們說台灣的電是 60 赫茲。
那是什麼在轉磁鐵？大多數電廠裡，是一具渦輪機：一個有葉片的輪子，被高速流動的東西推著轉。燃煤和核能電廠把水燒成高壓蒸汽，衝過渦輪；燃氣電廠在像噴射引擎的渦輪裡燒天然氣，很多還會利用剩下的熱再燒出蒸汽。在水壩，是落下的水推動渦輪；在風場，則是風。常見的發電方式裡，只有一種不一樣：太陽能板直接把陽光變成電，完全沒有會動的零件。
電從發電機出來後，沿著高高的電塔橫越全島。為了送得遠、少浪費，電壓會被升得非常高；台電最高的輸電線是 34 萬 5 千伏特。變電所再一層一層把它降下來，最後由你家附近的變壓器降到插座的 110 伏特。你家牆裡的電子並不是從發電廠一路跑過來的，它們只是在原地來回晃動，真正沿著電線飛快傳過來的是能量。
那台灣的電從哪裡來？2025 年，大約 48% 來自燃燒天然氣，35% 來自燃煤，13% 來自太陽能、風力等再生能源，大約 1% 來自核能。台灣最後一座核能機組在 2025 年 5 月停機。每一種選擇都有代價：燃煤和燃氣會排放二氧化碳，太陽和風則隨天氣來來去去。但除了太陽能板，它們都回到法拉第將近兩百年前發現的道理：讓磁鐵轉起來，電子就會動。
questions: Why is the electricity in the wall called alternating current?
Which common way of making electricity does not spin a generator?
answers: He discovered that moving a magnet near a coil of wire makes electricity flow in the wire, and that a magnet that is not moving makes no electricity.
Because as the magnet spins, its north and south poles take turns sweeping past the coils, so the current keeps changing direction. In Taiwan, it goes back and forth 60 times a second.
Solar panels. They turn sunlight directly into electricity with no moving parts.

vocab.ex: The hospital has a generator that starts when the power goes out.
vocab.exzh: 醫院有一台發電機，停電時會自動啟動。

vocab.ex: She stuck the photo to the fridge with a magnet.
vocab.exzh: 她用磁鐵把照片貼在冰箱上。

vocab.ex: A spring is a coil of metal wire.
vocab.exzh: 彈簧就是一圈圈的金屬線。

vocab.ex: The children watched the top spin on the table.
vocab.exzh: 孩子們看著陀螺在桌上旋轉。

vocab.ex: Falling water turns the turbine inside the dam.
vocab.exzh: 落下的水推動水壩裡的渦輪機。

vocab.ex: Steam rose from the hot bowl of noodles.
vocab.exzh: 熱騰騰的一碗麵冒著蒸汽。

vocab.ex: The outlets in your home supply alternating current.
vocab.exzh: 家裡的插座供應的是交流電。

vocab.ex: Don't plug too many things into one outlet.
vocab.exzh: 不要在同一個插座插太多東西。

quiz.q: What makes electricity flow in a generator's coils?
options: A magnet moving past the coils
A magnet sitting still next to the coils

quiz.q: How many complete back-and-forth cycles does the current in Taiwan's outlets make each second?
In a coal or nuclear power plant, what pushes the turbine?
Why is electricity sent across the island at a very high voltage?
options: So less energy is wasted on the way
So the electrons can reach your home faster
So the power lines can be made of plastic
So houses cannot use it by mistake

quiz.q: In 2025, which source made the largest share of Taiwan's electricity?

mix.lead_en: Share of all the electricity generated in Taiwan in 2025: about 289.7 billion kilowatt-hours. Gas passed coal as the biggest source in 2024.
mix.lead_zh: 2025 年全國總發電量約 2,897 億度，各種來源的占比如下。燃氣在 2024 年首度超過燃煤，成為最大的發電來源。
mix.note_en: Source: Energy Administration, Ministry of Economic Affairs, published on the Ministry of Environment's Energy Information Platform. “Other” is what is left after the four main groups.
mix.note_zh: 資料來源：經濟部能源署（刊於環境部能源資訊平台）。「其他」為四大類以外的剩餘部分。

plants.spin_en: Gas turbine, often plus a steam turbine
plants.spin_zh: 燃氣渦輪，常再加蒸汽渦輪
plants.text_en: Burns gas in a turbine like a jet engine. In a combined-cycle plant, the hot exhaust also boils water for a second, steam-driven turbine.
plants.text_zh: 在像噴射引擎的渦輪裡燒天然氣。複循環電廠還會用排出的熱氣燒水，推動第二具蒸汽渦輪。

plants.text_en: Burns coal to boil water, and the steam spins the turbine. For the same amount of electricity, coal releases more than twice as much carbon dioxide as natural gas.
plants.text_zh: 燒煤把水煮成蒸汽，蒸汽轉動渦輪。發同樣多的電，燃煤排放的二氧化碳是天然氣的兩倍以上。

plants.text_en: Splitting uranium atoms heats water into steam. Taiwan's last reactor, Maanshan Unit 2, shut down in May 2025. An August 2025 vote on restarting it did not pass because too few people voted.
plants.text_zh: 鈾原子分裂放出的熱把水變成蒸汽。台灣最後一座機組核三廠二號機在 2025 年 5 月停機；同年 8 月重啟核三的公投，因投票人數不足門檻而沒有通過。

plants.share_en: Part of renewables and pumped storage
plants.share_zh: 屬於再生能源與抽蓄水力
plants.text_en: Falling water spins the turbine. At Sun Moon Lake, Taipower pumps water uphill in the daytime with solar power and lets it fall to make electricity at night, like a giant battery.
plants.text_zh: 落下的水轉動水輪機。在日月潭，台電白天用太陽光電把水抽上去，晚上再放水發電，像一顆巨大的電池。

plants.text_en: The wind pushes long blades that turn a generator at the top of the tower. Some of Asia's largest offshore wind farms stand in the sea off Changhua.
plants.text_zh: 風推動長長的葉片，帶動塔頂的發電機。亞太地區最大的離岸風場之一，就在彰化外海。

plants.text_en: The one exception: solar panels turn light straight into electricity with no moving parts. How they do it is the next lesson.
plants.text_zh: 唯一的例外：太陽能板直接把光變成電，沒有任何會動的零件。它怎麼做到，是下一課的主題。

lessons.plants_note_en: Five of these six spin a generator. They differ only in what pushes the turbine, and in what that costs the air, the land, and the future.
lessons.plants_note_zh: 這六種裡有五種都在轉發電機，差別只在「是什麼推動渦輪」，以及它對空氣、土地和未來的代價。

myths.myth_en: The electricity in the wall is stored somewhere, like water in a tank.
myths.myth_zh: 插座裡的電是儲存在某個地方，像水塔裡的水。
myths.fact_en: Most of it is made at the very moment you use it. Power plants speed up and slow down all day to match what everyone is using right now.
myths.fact_zh: 大部分的電是在你使用的同一時刻才發出來的。發電廠一整天都在加速、減速，配合所有人此刻用了多少電。

myths.myth_en: A strong magnet next to a wire makes electricity.
myths.myth_zh: 強力磁鐵放在電線旁邊就會發電。
myths.fact_en: Only a changing magnetic field makes electricity. The magnet has to move, or the coil has to move. A magnet sitting still makes none at all.
myths.fact_zh: 只有「變化」的磁場才會發電：磁鐵要動，或線圈要動。靜止的磁鐵一點電也不會產生。

myths.myth_en: The electrons in your outlet traveled all the way from the power plant.
myths.myth_zh: 插座裡的電子是從發電廠一路跑過來的。
myths.fact_en: In alternating current, electrons just wiggle back and forth in place. What travels from the power plant is energy, carried along the wires very fast.
myths.fact_zh: 交流電的電子只在原地來回晃。從發電廠傳過來的是能量，沿著電線飛快地送到。

myths.myth_en: Taiwan's electricity is the same everywhere in the world.
myths.myth_zh: 全世界的插座都和台灣一樣。
myths.fact_en: Taiwan uses 110 volts at 60 hertz, like the United States. Most of Europe and mainland China use about 220 to 230 volts at 50 hertz, so travelers need the right adapter.
myths.fact_zh: 台灣用 110 伏特、60 赫茲，和美國相同；歐洲大部分國家和中國大陸用 220–230 伏特、50 赫茲，出國要帶合適的轉接頭與變壓器。

tricks.body_en: A magnet only makes electricity while it is moving. Spin it, and the electrons move; stop it, and they stop.
tricks.body_zh: 磁鐵只有在動的時候才發電。轉它，電子就動；停下來，電子也停。

tricks.title_zh: N 極推過去，S 極推回來
tricks.body_en: The poles take turns passing the coil, so the current keeps switching direction. That is AC.
tricks.body_zh: 兩個磁極輪流經過線圈，電流就一直換方向，這就是交流電。

tricks.body_en: Steam, gas, water, and wind are just different hands turning the crank. Only solar has no crank at all.
tricks.body_zh: 蒸汽、燃氣、水和風，只是換了不同的手在搖同一根曲柄；只有太陽能完全沒有曲柄。

tricks.title_en: High on the road, low at home
tricks.title_zh: 路上用高壓，到家變低壓
tricks.body_en: Electricity travels at hundreds of thousands of volts to waste less, then steps down to 110 volts for your home.
tricks.body_zh: 電在路上用幾十萬伏特傳送以減少浪費，到家前再降成 110 伏特。

materials.en: About 10 meters of thin enameled copper wire (magnet wire)
materials.zh: 約 10 公尺的細漆包銅線

materials.en: A cardboard tube, such as a toilet-paper roll
materials.zh: 一個紙筒（例如衛生紙捲筒）

materials.en: A strong bar magnet that fits inside the tube
materials.zh: 一根放得進紙筒的強力磁棒
三用電表，或一個指南針

steps.en: Wind the wire around the tube at least 100 times, keeping the turns close together. Tape the coil so it does not unwind, and leave about 30 centimeters free at each end.
steps.zh: 把銅線在紙筒上繞至少 100 圈，一圈緊挨一圈，用膠帶固定，兩端各留約 30 公分。

steps.en: Sand the last 2 centimeters of each end until the copper shines. The colored coating does not carry electricity.
steps.zh: 用砂紙把兩端最後 2 公分磨到露出亮亮的銅色；外面那層漆不導電。

steps.en: Connect the two ends to a multimeter set to its smallest voltage range. (No meter? Wrap the ends 20 times around a compass instead and watch the needle.)
steps.zh: 兩端接到三用電表，轉到最小的電壓檔。（沒有電表？把兩端在指南針上繞 20 圈，看指針。）

steps.en: Push the magnet quickly into the tube. Watch the reading jump. Hold the magnet still inside: the reading drops back to zero.
steps.zh: 把磁鐵快速推進紙筒，讀數會跳一下；把磁鐵停在裡面不動，讀數又回到零。

steps.en: Pull the magnet out. The reading jumps the other way. Push it in and out over and over: you have made alternating current.
steps.zh: 把磁鐵拉出來，讀數往反方向跳。一進一出來回做：你做出的就是交流電。

steps.en: Try it faster and slower. Which gives the bigger reading?
steps.zh: 快一點、慢一點各試試看，哪一種讀數比較大？

activities.tip_en: Strong magnets can pinch fingers, so an adult should handle them. Keep magnets away from phones, bank cards, and anyone with a pacemaker, and never let small children put magnets in their mouths. The reading is tiny, only thousandths of a volt, which is why power plants spin magnets so fast in huge coils.
activities.tip_zh: 強力磁鐵會夾傷手指，請由大人拿取。磁鐵要遠離手機、金融卡和裝心律調節器的人，也絕不能讓小孩放進嘴裡。讀數非常小，只有千分之幾伏特，這也是電廠要在巨大的線圈裡把磁鐵轉得那麼快的原因。

activities.title_zh: 順著電線找電從哪裡來

materials.en: A walk around the school or neighborhood (with an adult)
materials.zh: 在校園或社區走一圈（大人陪同）

materials.en: A notebook for a simple map
materials.zh: 一本可以畫簡單地圖的筆記本

steps.en: Start at a classroom outlet. Where do the wires go? Look for the electrical panel with the switches (breakers), but do not open it.
steps.zh: 從教室的插座開始：電線往哪裡去？找找看有開關（斷路器）的配電箱，但不要打開。

steps.en: Go outside and find where the power comes into the building, and the transformer nearby: a gray barrel on a pole or a green box on the ground.
steps.zh: 到戶外找電從哪裡進入大樓，以及附近的變壓器：電線桿上的灰色圓桶，或地上的綠色箱子。

steps.en: Follow the lines along the street with your eyes. Can you see tall towers in the distance? Those carry the high-voltage lines.
steps.zh: 用眼睛順著街上的電線看過去。遠方看得到高高的電塔嗎？那就是高壓輸電線。

steps.en: Draw the path: outlet → panel → transformer → power lines → substation → power plant. Write the voltage at each step that you learned in the reading.
steps.zh: 畫出路線：插座 → 配電箱 → 變壓器 → 電線 → 變電所 → 發電廠，並寫上課文裡學到的各段電壓。

steps.en: Back in class, look up Taipower's live data, which shows how much each power plant is making right now, updated every 10 minutes.
steps.zh: 回到教室，查台電的即時資料：每 10 分鐘更新一次，顯示每座電廠此刻發多少電。

activities.tip_en: Look, but never touch. Stay far away from substations, transformer boxes, and fallen power lines, and never fly a kite or climb a tree near power lines.
activities.tip_zh: 只看不碰。遠離變電所、變壓器箱和掉落的電線；絕不在電線附近放風箏或爬樹。

safety.en: Never put anything except a plug into an outlet, and never touch a plug with wet hands. The electricity in the wall can seriously hurt or kill you.
safety.zh: 插座只插插頭，絕不放進其他東西；手濕的時候絕不碰插頭。插座裡的電會造成重傷甚至致命。

safety.en: Stay away from fallen power lines, especially after a typhoon. Tell an adult and call Taipower; do not go near them.
safety.zh: 遠離掉落的電線，颱風過後尤其要小心。告訴大人並通報台電，不要靠近。

safety.en: Never fly kites, drones, or balloons near power lines, and never climb electric towers or poles.
safety.zh: 絕不在電線附近放風箏、無人機或氣球，也絕不攀爬電塔或電線桿。

safety.en: A gasoline generator must never be run indoors or in a garage. Its exhaust contains carbon monoxide, a gas you cannot see or smell that can kill.
safety.zh: 汽油發電機絕不能在室內或車庫裡運轉。它的廢氣含有一氧化碳，看不見也聞不到，會致命。

safety.en: Strong magnets can pinch skin and are very dangerous if swallowed. Keep them away from young children.
safety.zh: 強力磁鐵會夾傷皮膚，誤吞非常危險，要放在幼兒拿不到的地方。
